edition: Issue 040: The phone call finally happens — Luxon and Wong make it an hour and call it 'really lovely', Footrot Flats turns 50, and a Beach Fern funds her tour one subscription at a time
tagline: Your 3-minute Tuesday reset: an hour-long meeting between the man who ruled her out and the woman who out-waited him, Wal Footrot's farm celebrating half a century as the country's most functional institution, and the funding model of Olympic sport explained by its most creative employee.

stories.headline: Luxon makes the call he swore he never would — an hour with Qiulae Wong, now described as 'really lovely'
stories.summary: Christopher Luxon spent an hour in his office with Opportunity leader Qiulae Wong on Monday night after ruling her party out all campaign, calling the meeting 'very positive, very constructive' and 'really lovely', pointing to shared KiwiSaver ground, as National's first post-election caucus sat down and the country keeps waiting on special votes (official results 27 November).

body.text: For most of the campaign, Christopher Luxon's position on Opportunity leader Qiulae Wong was a one-word answer: no. On Monday night, he spent an hour with her in his office. Luxon described the meeting before National's first post-election caucus on Tuesday as 'very positive, very constructive' and, in the phrase that will be doing heavy lifting for the next few weeks, 'really lovely' — a chance, he said, 'to get to know her and to start to build a relationship together'. He pointed to KiwiSaver as an area where the two parties agree. Pressed on whether he is open to a governing deal with Opportunity, Luxon leaned first on National's established relationships with ACT and New Zealand First, but he acknowledged what the final count may still deliver: 'New Zealanders won't thank us for going back to an election and back to the polls again.' All of it happens while special votes stay uncounted, with official results on 27 November, and Tuesday's new-MP school saw Opportunity's fresh intake learning how Parliament works.

Nine months of 'absolutely not, over my dead coalition agreement' — and now it's 'really lovely'. This is the fastest turn-around since the All Blacks took a lead, and somewhere in Wellington a speechwriter is sketching save-the-date cards. Watch the romantic choreography: Luxon cited KiwiSaver as the shared love language, which must be thrilling news for everyone who assumed the connection was all about land value tax. Wong, for her part, spoke to the largest party first exactly as promised — a woman who makes a negotiation point out of being on time. Both sides are now at that giddy stage where every word is a signal: 'really lovely' sits somewhere between a wet bus ticket and a wedding invitation. Parliament meanwhile trundles on under the caretaker convention, which is a fancy way of saying everyone is being very romantic and committing to absolutely nothing. Roll on the official results — the only poll that actually counts.

RNZ (10 Nov 2026, 'Very constructive conversation: Luxon holds hour-long meeting with Opportunity's Qiulae Wong'): Luxon spent an hour with Wong in his office on Monday night, after repeatedly ruling out working with her party during the campaign; his quotes — 'We had a very positive, very constructive conversation', 'a great opportunity to get to know her and to start to build a relationship together', the meeting was 'really lovely', and KiwiSaver was an area of agreement; asked whether he was open to a governing deal he pointed first to National's relationship with ACT and NZ First but acknowledged the prospect of a hung Parliament on the final count: 'New Zealanders won't thank us for going back to an election and back to the polls again.' NZ Herald (10 Nov, election-2026 live updates): 'Luxon and Wong had very positive, constructive first meeting last night'; National and Labour each held their first caucus meetings on Tuesday. RNZ election live blog (10 Nov): tensions rising over vote-splitting campaigns, with outgoing minister Chris Bishop slamming vote-splitting as he farewelled Parliament. Context carried from RNZ/The Conversation (8 Nov): official results 27 November; RNZ (Lauren Crimp, 8 Nov): new-MP school begins Tuesday 10 November.

stories.headline: Footrot Flats turns 50 and the farm is still the most functional institution in the country
stories.summary: It's 50 years since Kiwis first met Wal Footrot and his 'faithful, if somewhat opinionated' dog: the anniversary collection 'Here's to the Good Times!' lands today, Murray Ball's son Mason joins RNZ's Nine to Noon, and the 1986 film The Dog's Tale and Dave Dobbyn's 'Slice of Heaven' mark 40 years beside it.

body.text: For half a century, the most reliably governed territory in New Zealand has been a fictional sheep farm in the Rangitikei. Footrot Flats, the strip Murray Ball began in 1976, is 50 this year, and the family is marking it with a new coffee-table collection, 'Footrot Flats: Here's to the Good Times!', out on 10 November — a celebration put together by Murray's son Mason Ball, who joins RNZ's Nine to Noon on Tuesday to talk about the legacy. The anniversary lands in good company: 2026 also marks 40 years since the animated feature The Dog's Tale, with Dave Dobbyn's 'Slice of Heaven' riding the film to the top of the charts — RNZ marked the occasion with a re-mastered trailer. Murray Ball, who died in 2017, drew the strip from a farm near Gisborne to the end of his life. And the Dog, in case fifty years have dulled the memory, remains the only farmhand ever promoted above his owner with a straight face.

Wal Footrot's farm has now outlasted every government of the last half-century and, on current form, is well placed to outlast the next one. The Dog — whose official role is, as readers know, general in charge of everything — has demonstrated for fifty years that the one who barks loudest doesn't always win, which is presumably why politicians are never allowed near the kelpies. The farm's eternal laws hold steady: sheep are stupid but loyal, the Major is wrong about everything, and no matter how wet it gets, someone will still ask if you've tried ring-drenching. This week, Wellington's most romantic sentence is 'it was really lovely' — and still the country's most stable relationship remains Rangi and Wal arguing about fencing. Here's to fifty more years of the only public institution where the dog runs the place and everyone is absolutely fine with it.

RNZ Nine to Noon (10 Nov 2026, 'Footrot at 50'): 'It's been 50 years since Kiwis were first introduced to Wal Footrot and his faithful, if somewhat opinionated, dog'; the new collection 'Footrot Flats: Here's to the Good Times!' celebrates the strip's 50th anniversary and Murray's son Mason Ball joins the programme. Publisher metadata (Hachette Australia, release date 10 November 2026, ISBN 9780733655371, 192pp hardcover): 'Celebrate 50 years of Wal, Dog, and farming fun!' RNZ (2026, '40 years since Slice of Heaven — Footrot Flats back to celebrate'): the 1986 film The Dog's Tale and its theme tune mark 40 years, with a re-mastered trailer released on the day the song sat top of the charts. Publisher biography (Hachette): Murray Ball returned to New Zealand in 1974 and created Footrot Flats, living on a farm on the outskirts of Gisborne until he passed away in 2017.

stories.headline: 'Same as if someone was sponsored by Adidas': Beach Fern Olivia MacDonald funds her tour from the OnlyFans 'athlete side'
stories.summary: Beach Fern Olivia MacDonald says joining OnlyFans' growing 'athlete side' five months ago — signing bonus and regular payments included — has been a 'game changer': she has often worked two jobs, High Performance Sport NZ funding has its limits, and 'there's no way I would have been able to compete otherwise'.

body.text: Beach Fern Olivia MacDonald has a simple description for the sponsor that now helps fund her beach volleyball career: 'It's the same as if someone was sponsored by Adidas.' The sponsor is OnlyFans. Five months ago the 30-year-old joined the platform's 'athlete side' — the growing branch where professional athletes monetise their careers — and received a signing bonus in the process, with regular payments on top. She is explicit about what the account is: 'I'm not on the other side of the OnlyFans, which is often what people just assume.' Her posts are her playing her sport — 'it's a bikini sport, so you can find photos of me' — plus the OnlyFans merch reels the social media requirements call for, and a cardio session filmed up Mount Maunganui for OnlyFans TV. And she is blunt about why: getting to the international tournaments she needs has been a constant struggle. 'I've often worked two jobs... if that's what you want to do, you've got to sacrifice something and make it happen.' High Performance Sport NZ funding has improved in recent years and goes towards travel, but it is limited: 'We don't have a whole lot of sponsors chomping at the bit to sponsor beach volleyball.' The result: 'There's no way I would have been able to compete otherwise. I was able to fund my partner and I just to be able to get to some events once our regular funding ran dry.'

There's a funding gap, and then there's the gap so wide OnlyFans has to fill it for a Beach Fern: the sponsors are chomping at the bit all right, they're just subscription-based. Olivia MacDonald has done the arithmetic the funding bodies haven't — two jobs plus a signing bonus moves you further than one small grant and a prayer. The beautiful absurdity: the sport's most reliable backer is the platform everyone assumed she wouldn't touch, and her content is just her doing her actual job, on a beach, in the merch. Meanwhile the elite funding system that can't quite cover her flights is presumably still in a meeting about it. She's got the hustle, the honesty and the merch — fund the athletes properly, New Zealand, because the alternative is our medal hopes depending on a good camera angle, and that's a strange way to run a high-performance programme.

RNZ (Bridget Tunnicliffe, 9 Nov 2026, ''Athlete side' of OnlyFans helps fund beach volleyball Olivia MacDonald star's career'): MacDonald, 30, joined the athlete side of OnlyFans five months ago, receiving a signing bonus plus regular payments and a bonus system tied to interviews and wearing the merch; quotes — 'It's the same as if someone was sponsored by Adidas', 'I'm not on the other side of the OnlyFans, which is often what people just assume', 'I've often worked two jobs... you've got to sacrifice something and make it happen', 'We don't have a whole lot of sponsors chomping at the bit to sponsor beach volleyball', 'There's no way I would have been able to compete otherwise. I was able to fund my partner and I just to be able to get to some events once our regular funding ran dry.'; posts include bikini-sport photos, OnlyFans merch reels (social media requirements) and a Mount Maunganui cardio video on OnlyFans TV; High Performance Sport NZ funding improved over recent years and goes towards travel, but remains limited; OnlyFans, founded 2016, is a subscription platform where fans pay for exclusive photos, videos and live streams.

affiliate_cta.headline: Backing a good thing? The calm look-around before you commit.
affiliate_cta.body: Today's edition is about support in its many forms: a party phoning someone it spent a year ruling out, a farm dog who never got the memo that he's meant to take orders, and an athlete funding her season out of her own back pocket.
